JOHANNESBURG, Aug 24 : South Africa have released fullback Quan Horn and prop Boan Venter from the Springbok squad to play for provincial side Lions against New Zealand at Ellis Park on Tuesday. • Venter was named on Monday among the replacements and is in line to make his Lions debut after signing for them, having played for Edinburgh in Scotland. • There could also be a debut for former Springbok loose forward Sikhumbuzo Notshe, who previously played club rugby in France and is also on the bench. • The Lions’ other Springbok squad member, scrumhalf Morné van den Berg, has not been released, increasing his chances of a run out against the All Blacks in Saturday’s second test in Cape Town.

Replacements: 16-Morne Brandon, 17-Boan Venter, 18-RF Schoeman, 19-Hyron Andrews, 20-Sikhumbuzo Notshe, 21-JC Pretorius, 22-Haashim Pead, 23-Boeta Chamberlain.

RENNES, France, Aug 24 : Paris Saint-Germain players can ill afford to cruise through the season as coach Luis Enrique warned he expected them to play out of their comfort zone. The PSG coach took off both Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at halftime of their opening game of the new Ligue 1 season, bringing on Mika Godts and Ferran Torres, who scored twice to salvage a point at Stade Rennais on Sunday. "Football is like that. Paris Saint-Germain have won nothing, nothing," he said of the new season where they defend not only their Ligue 1 title but chase a third successive Champions League victory. "If you think about what you've won, you're not going to win anything! There is no credit. You have to show every day, every match, every training session, that you're ready. Otherwise, it's easy to relax and start slipping.

"I wasn't brought up that way. We are always looking to win, and to keep winning, you have to step outside your comfort zone. Is that clear?" PSG, who won the European Super Cup this month but lost the French version to Racing Lens, played a sluggish first half at Rennes and were 2-0 down at the break. But new Spanish signing Ferran Torres, who netted the winner in last month's World Cup final, came on for Dembélé and scored twice to ensure a point for the Parisians. "He wasn't bad, was he? He scored two goals, but I'm happy with everyone who came on in a very difficult match because we had a lot of trouble controlling Rennes in the first half," Luis Enrique said. "They were good on the counterattack and scored two wonderful goals. It was complicated, but it's important for me to see that so many players are ready. "We sign players to go on a long journey with them. It's very positive for him and we're very happy," he said of Ferran Torres' debut. "We're always looking to find the best players for every match. Places in the team will be more difficult to get than last year, and that's our ambition. "I think we had a very good transfer window, and we're still open to different possibilities. Everyone knows how difficult it is for a team to keep winning. And clearly, we still need to improve."

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Christopher Cushing)

Source: Reuters

ZANDVOORT, Netherlands, Aug 24 : McLaren have taken a big step forward and Mercedes no longer have the quickest car in Formula One, championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix. McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris celebrated his second win in a row from pole position at Zandvoort, with Antonelli and Mercedes teammate George Russell second and third ahead of Ferrari pair Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. "We’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid," said Antonelli, who won five races in a row earlier in the season. "We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought."

Norris, who lost out to Antonelli at the race restart and then had to overtake him on track, questioned that assertion however. "I don’t think it’s true. I think if I didn’t get Kimi when I overtook him, I don’t think I would have won the race," he said. "For once I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference. "We certainly have a car now capable of beating them ... but I think they have a better all-round performing car than what we do." Zandvoort, and Budapest's Hungaroring before that, played to McLaren's strengths but some of the tracks coming up may be less favourable. Ferrari can be expected to go well at their home grand prix at Monza early next month, with upgrades in the pipeline, while Antonelli faces hefty grid penalties for an engine change. A TOUGHER RIDE Mercedes are still way ahead of Ferrari and McLaren in the constructors' championship and scored more points (46 to McLaren's 43 and Ferrari's 31) than anyone else over the weekend. "We have a strong car in certain areas. It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere," said Norris. "We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that’s a good thing. "But the advantage that they (Mercedes) have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say 'yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. "I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship," added the Briton, who is 83 points behind Antonelli with another 11 rounds remaining unless the situation in the Middle East forces a calendar change. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said cost-cap restrictions meant Mercedes did not have the money to put developments on the car as fast as they might like to. "We are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points," he told reporters. "So the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year." McLaren principal Andrea Stella said he expected Mercedes to accelerate their car's development regardless. "I'm sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track," said the Italian. "And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I'm just pretty sure that they will have upgrades."

Source: Reuters

BEIJING, Aug 24 : Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi on Monday unveiled a new version of its in-house Xring smartphone processor, betting that deeper control over key components will help strengthen its supply chain and reduce reliance on external chip suppliers. The introduction of Xring O3 comes a year after Xiaomi launched its first proprietary smartphone processor, the Xring O1, marking the latest step in the world's third-largest smartphone vendor's push to join rivals such as Apple, Samsung Electronics and Huawei in developing its own chips. TSMC will manufacture the new chip using its 3-nanometre production technology, two people familiar with the matter said. One of the sources said the chip is expected to power Xiaomi's upcoming flagship folding phone, with a shipment target of 200,000 to 300,000 units.

Xiaomi and TSMC did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the chip's manufacturer, production technology or shipment targets. Smartphone processors, or system-on-chips (SoC), integrate computing, graphics, AI processing and imaging functions into a single component.  Xiaomi's chip push reflects a broader industry trend as device makers seek to differentiate products and lessen dependence on suppliers such as Qualcomm and MediaTek amid intensifying competition in premium smartphones. Xiaomi said during an earnings call last week that cumulative shipments of devices powered by the Xring O1, including smartphones, tablets and watches, had surpassed 1 million units since its launch. Xiaomi has sold about 150,000 smartphones based on the Xring O1 chip since its May 2025 launch, according to the sources.

FAST

MELBOURNE, Aug 24 : Normal service resumed for Australia as their formidable bowling unit hit their marks in the second test against Bangladesh in Mackay but questions remain over a batting order that continues to misfire at the top. Australia's innings and 51-run victory was a strong comeback from the Darwin defeat as pace leaders Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins blasted away the tourists' batters in a timely reminder of their quality ahead of a tough, three-test tour of South Africa in October. Australia's batting has left selectors with a headache, though, and struggling number three Marnus Labuschagne may be nervous about his place in the squad for South Africa. South Africa-born Labuschagne was already under major scrutiny after two poor dismissals in Darwin before he was bowled for four in Mackay by Shoriful Islam, the ball catching his thigh pad before hitting the stumps.

Upon his dismissal, Labuschagne gave the look of a man forsaken by the cricketing gods and later took scissors to his thigh pad in an unusual gear modification. But behind the theatrics was a batter who had strayed far across his crease and given Shoriful a look at leg stump, further evidence for pundits of a need for change. "There's some technical deficiency there, but he's making the margin for error for the bowlers too great," said former Australia captain Ricky Ponting. "It's well and truly time to have a look at somebody else." Labuschagne's exit would be the second top-order batter dropped in two matches after opener Jake Weatherald was dumped in the wake of the fiasco in Darwin, where Australia fell to a shock nine-wicket defeat. Weatherald's replacement Matt Renshaw hardly inspired in his first test in over three years, falling for eight with a nick to the slips, but he will be afforded time to bed into the role. Whether Travis Head should accompany him at the top of the order remains a troublesome question for selectors. Moved up from the middle order for the Ashes as Usman Khawaja struggled with injury, Head has remained there despite not really being seen as a proper opener. Some former players, including Mark Waugh, want Head back down in the middle order but that would mean gambling with two unproven openers against South Africa, who beat Australia for the World Test Championship title last year. With runs in Darwin and Mackay, Cameron Green has belatedly shored up his spot at number five so bringing Head back down would mean upsetting the formula of having wicketkeeper Alex Carey at six and the second all-rounder Beau Webster at seven. Selectors picked a thin 13-man squad for the Bangladesh series but are expected to take at least 16 to South Africa and include additional batting cover. Quite who gets the nod among the batters on the fringes is far from certain, with no real stand-out candidates having emerged. Carey said there was no urgency to shake up Australia's batting lineup further. "I think we felt a little bit like we left some runs out there (against Bangladesh), so we are always looking to improve as a batting unit," he told reporters in Mackay. "We are hungry. We are working really hard."

Source: Reuters

Aug 24 : Sonova launched its third hearing-aid platform utilising real-time AI on Monday, its latest effort to strengthen its position in a market that relies on rapid technology upgrades to shorten replacement cycles and attract first-time users. The Swiss company was the first one to roll out a hearing aid that used real-time AI to separate speech from background noise in 2024. Anders Rosengren, the head of research and development at Sonova, said the new Phonak EON platform offers a smaller, lighter device with an advanced AI that makes speech twice as understandable while requiring less listening effort. The new platform is likely to be viewed as an important factor for Sonova to reach its medium-term growth targets that were met with investor scepticism in March.

"We expect EON adoption to build quickly among both replacement and new customers," said Oliver Lux, president of Sonova's EMEA and Latin America regions. While Sonova did not disclose pricing details, Lux said EON was designed to support the company's premium market positioning at launch. Monday's U.S. launch will be followed by Australia and key European markets including Germany, France, Italy and Britain in mid-September, before a broader global roll-out. Sonova continues to see positive market dynamics across its key markets, and especially in Asia-Pacific and Latin America, Lux said. Under CEO Eric Bernard, who took office last September, Sonova has increasingly highlighted Asia-Pacific as a key growth region, where it seeks to expand volumes and strengthen its presence in faster-growing markets that are buoyed by ageing populations.

SYDNEY: New Zealand's conservative coalition government will introduce a Bill in parliament on Monday (Aug 24) that seeks to ban children under 16 from using social media, and proposes fines of up to 10 per cent of a platform's global revenue for non-compliance. The Bill would require social media platforms to take reasonable steps to verify users' ages, including by using existing account information, facial technology and digital identity documents. "We simply cannot accept the harm being done to a generation of New Zealand children," Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said in a statement. "Social media is exposing them to harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they are not equipped to deal with, and it's affecting their family life, mental health, sleep, and education," Luxon said.

It was not immediately clear if the bill would garner sufficient support to pass through Parliament, with one of Luxon's coalition partners, the New Zealand First party, saying it would not support it. "We have been concerned with the proposed legislation and the direction and slippery slope that legislation like this will inevitably take our country," New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, who is also the country's foreign minister, said in a post on X. In December, Australia became the world's first country to ban social media for children under 16, blocking them from platforms including TikTok, Alphabet's YouTube and Meta's Instagram and Facebook. That legislation had been a "colossal failure," Peters said, adding that keeping children off social media should be the responsibility of parents. "I won't pretend that it will be simple or that it will be perfect," Luxon said at an event. "We won't get every single child off social media. Some will always find ways around it, but frankly, it's just way too important not to at least try."
